title: 4SD0 exam-style questions written for this lesson (lesson 111)
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y11 lesson 111 (4SD0 exam-style questions written for this lesson (portal question sheet with mark scheme))
intro: Lesson 111: Revision: B3 cell division, variation and natural selection. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Explain how a population of insects becomes resistant to a pesticide. Portal response box.
questions.a: Variation in the population (1); due to a mutation (1); pesticide kills non-resistant insects (1); resistant insects survive (1); reproduce and pass on the allele (1); over many generations most are resistant (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'There is variation in the insect population caused by mutation.'

questions.q: Why is meiosis needed before fertilisation?
questions.a: Halves the chromosome number (1) so the zygote has the normal diploid number (1); produces variation (1)

questions.q: Suggest two ways hospitals reduce antibiotic resistance.
questions.a: Prescribe only when needed; patients finish courses; hygiene to stop spread

questions.q: Explain how antibiotic resistance spreads in a population of bacteria.
questions.a: Random mutation gives resistance (1); antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria (1); resistant bacteria survive and reproduce (1); pass on the resistance allele/population becomes resistant (1)
questions.model: Four links: mutation, selection by antibiotic, survival and reproduction, inheritance.

questions.q: State two differences between mitosis and meiosis.
questions.a: Mitosis 2 cells, meiosis 4; mitosis identical, meiosis different (or diploid vs haploid)

questions.q: Give an example of environmental variation.
questions.a: Scars, language, a plant's height in poor soil
